answer.label: Collected by Spurgeon — origin unconfirmed
answer.sourceLine: Wikiquote assigns this proverb to The Salt-Cellars, volume 1, page 89. A second quotation reference gives 1889, while Wikiquote’s section labels the collection 1885; the checked Google Books catalog confirms an 1889 edition but did not expose the passage. The wording is credibly associated with Spurgeon’s collection; direct page inspection and original authorship remain unconfirmed.

author.name: Charles Haddon Spurgeon
author.heading: About Charles Haddon Spurgeon
author.bio: Charles Haddon Spurgeon was a British Baptist preacher associated with London’s Metropolitan Tabernacle. His sermons and devotional books reached readers far beyond his congregation. Collections such as The Salt-Cellars also transmitted proverbs, so a phrase appearing in his books need not be his invention.

lead: The Salt-Cellars is a collection of proverbs with accompanying notes. Inclusion in that sort of collection documents use and transmission, not necessarily invention. Conflicting secondary edition dates are therefore kept visible rather than converted into a claimed first publication. Wikiquote source reference ↗
